question: Which items will Thornmere District Council refuse to collect as bulky waste?
statement: The Council does not collect building rubble, car parts, tyres, gas bottles or asbestos as bulky waste [S5].
rationale: S5 lists exactly these excluded items in almost the same words.

question: How much is the Thornmere fixed penalty for repeated recycling contamination if it is paid within 14 days?
statement: According to [S2], the £80 fixed penalty notice for repeated contamination is reduced to £40 if it is paid within 14 days.
rationale: S2 says the penalty is reduced to £50, not £40, so the changed amount is not supported.

question: Who can apply for a 240-litre grey bin in Thornmere, and on which form?
statement: [S2] Households with at least six residents may request the larger 240-litre grey bin by sending form WR-14 together with proof of how many people live there.
rationale: S2 states that households of six or more people can apply for a 240-litre grey bin on form WR-14 with proof of the number of residents.

question: Does Thornmere collect glass bottles from the kerbside?
statement: Yes, glass is collected from the kerbside in Thornmere [S5].
rationale: S5 says glass is not collected from the kerbside, so the statement reverses the passage.

question: What is the latest time Thornmere residents can put their containers at the kerb on collection day?
statement: Containers should be at the kerbside by 6:30 am on your collection day [S1].
rationale: S1 gives the deadline as 06:30, which is the same time as 6:30 am.

question: Until when can a Thornmere bulky waste booking be cancelled without losing the charge?
statement: A bulky waste booking can be cancelled at no cost until 12:00 on the working day before collection day; if you cancel any later, the fee is not given back [S3].
rationale: S3 says cancellation is free until 12:00 on the working day before the collection and that the charge is not refunded after that.

question: Who leads the Environmental Services team that runs Thornmere's waste collections?
statement: The Environmental Services team that runs the service is led by Daniel Ferreira-Hughes [S2].
rationale: S2 names Ruth Abernathy-Coles as head of the team, while Daniel Ferreira-Hughes is the Clinical Waste Officer in S1, so the role is given to the wrong person.

question: What happens after a Thornmere household receives a third yellow tag for contaminated recycling within 12 months?
statement: After a third yellow tag in any 12-month period, an Education Officer visits the household to explain the rules [S1].
rationale: S1 contains this sentence almost word for word.

question: Can Thornmere residents pick up free compost at the Sandpiper Road Household Recycling Centre?
statement: According to [S5], residents can collect free compost made from the district's garden waste at the Sandpiper Road centre.
rationale: No passage says that compost is given out at Sandpiper Road or anywhere else.

question: How should household batteries be set out for collection in Thornmere?
statement: According to [S4], batteries go in a clear bag that is sealed and left on top of the lid of the blue bin.
rationale: S4 tells residents to put household batteries in a clear sealed bag on top of the blue bin lid.

question: How many van permits can a single Thornmere household get each year for the Sandpiper Road centre?
statement: Each household can receive up to 15 van permits per year for the Household Recycling Centre [S3].
rationale: S3 allows up to 12 van permits per household per year, not 15.

question: How short must a real Christmas tree be cut for the Thornmere garden waste collection in January 2027?
statement: Real trees need to be cut into pieces no longer than 120 cm, with all decorations, pots and stands removed [S3].
rationale: S3 sets the limit at 1.2 metres, which is the same length as 120 cm, and requires decorations, pots and stands to be removed.

question: Will Thornmere's garden waste crews take artificial Christmas trees in January 2027?
statement: Yes, artificial Christmas trees are accepted in the tree collection as well as real ones [S2].
rationale: S2 states that artificial trees are not accepted, so the statement reverses it.

question: Is a Thornmere garden waste subscriber who moves to a new address inside the district entitled to a refund?
statement: No. A move within the district does not qualify for a refund, because the garden waste subscription transfers with you to the new address [S5].
rationale: S5 says moves within the district do not qualify because the subscription moves with the resident to the new address.

question: How is the Dunmarra instalment plan split for courses of 24 weeks or more?
statement: Per [S2], students on a course lasting 24 weeks or longer can split the fee into three payments: 40% at booking, 30% before week 8 begins and another 30% before week 16 begins.
rationale: S2 describes three instalments of 40% at booking, 30% before week 8 and 30% before week 16 for courses of 24 weeks or more.

question: Which Dunmarra staff member handles questions about accommodation and certificates?
statement: Questions about accommodation and certificates are handled by the Director of Studies, Ines Moreau-Batista [S1].
rationale: S1 gives these questions to the Student Services Manager, Kofi Adjei-Brandt, while Ines Moreau-Batista organises teaching, so the task is given to the wrong person.

question: What document must Dunmarra students aged 16 or 17 bring on their first day?
statement: Students aged 16 or 17 must bring the parental consent form U18, signed by a parent or guardian, on their first day [S4].
rationale: S4 states this requirement in nearly the same words.

question: How far ahead of the exam date does registration for a Dunmarra Proficiency Test session close?
statement: Registration for each DPT session closes eight weeks before the exam date [S5].
rationale: S3 and S5 both say registration closes six weeks before the exam date, not eight.

question: What refund does Dunmarra give if a student's visa application is refused?
statement: If the student visa is refused, Dunmarra returns everything paid apart from a €150 administration charge, as long as the student sends a copy of the refusal letter within 10 days of the decision date [S3].
rationale: S3 says all fees are refunded except a €150 administration charge if the refusal letter is sent within 10 days of the decision.

question: Are Dunmarra lessons that fall on a public holiday made up later?
statement: Yes, lessons that fall on a public holiday are made up later in the course [S4].
rationale: S4 says lessons on public holidays are not made up or refunded, so the statement reverses it.

question: How much does a one-way transfer from Dunmarra Airport cost?
statement: A one-way transfer from Dunmarra Airport to your accommodation costs seventy euros [S3].
rationale: S3 gives the one-way transfer price as €70, the same value as seventy euros.

question: What tuition discount applies to a Dunmarra Standard course booking of 24 weeks?
statement: As [S2] explains, students who book 24 weeks or more receive a 20% discount on tuition.
rationale: S2 gives a 15% discount for bookings of 24 weeks or more, not 20%.

question: What does a Dunmarra student get back after leaving a course early?
statement: Early leavers are not given cash; they receive a credit note for the unused full weeks of tuition, which can be spent on any course at the Centre and stays valid for 12 months from the date it is issued [S1].
rationale: S1 says there are no cash refunds after the start and that early leavers get a credit note for unused full weeks, usable on any course for 12 months.

question: Can Dunmarra students add private one-to-one lessons to their course?
statement: Yes, one-to-one private lessons can be added to any course for €52 per hour [S2].
rationale: None of the passages mentions private or one-to-one lessons or an hourly price for them.

question: What happens at Dunmarra Language Centre if a student has not done the online placement test in time?
statement: If you have not taken the online test at least three days before your first lesson, you will take a paper test at 08:30 on your first Monday and start lessons one day later [S1].
rationale: S1 states the three-day deadline and the paper test at 08:30 on the first Monday with lessons starting one day later, in nearly the same words.

question: Which Dunmarra classes have a maximum of 8 students?
statement: The Evening course classes are the ones capped at 8 students [S5].
rationale: S5 gives the limit of 8 to the Intensive course's afternoon workshops, while Evening classes have a maximum of 12.

question: What minimum attendance must Dunmarra students on a student visa keep?
statement: Students who hold a student visa must attend at least 75% of their lessons [S1].
rationale: S1 sets the minimum for student-visa holders at 85%, not 75%.

question: How many minutes late can a Dunmarra student be before being marked absent for the first lesson of the day?
statement: Anyone who turns up more than 15 minutes late is recorded as absent for the day's first lesson [S5].
rationale: S5 says students who arrive more than 15 minutes late are marked absent for the first lesson of the day.

question: On which Gullstone pontoons is the 2026–27 licence fee €350 per metre?
statement: The €350-per-metre licence fee applies to pontoons A to E [S1].
rationale: S1 charges €350 per metre on pontoons F to H, while pontoons A to E pay €395, so the rate is attached to the wrong pontoons.

question: What do berth holders and visitors each pay to use the Gullstone black water pump-out?
statement: Berth holders can use the pump-out at the end of pontoon D without paying anything [S1], whereas visiting boats are charged €15 each time they use it [S3].
rationale: S1 says the pump-out at the end of pontoon D is free for berth holders and S3 says visitors pay €15 per use, so each part is stated in the cited passage.

question: What permit does Gullstone Harbour Marina require for welding on the pontoons, and how early must it be requested?
statement: Hot work is not allowed on the pontoons without a Hot Work Permit (form HW-3) from the Harbour Master, which must be requested at least 24 hours in advance [S5].
rationale: S5 contains this rule almost word for word.

question: What speed limit applies in the approach channel to Gullstone Harbour Marina?
statement: The speed limit is 10 knots in the approach channel [S1].
rationale: S1 sets the approach channel limit at 5 knots, not 10.

question: Is there a pressure-wash bay for visiting boats at Gullstone?
statement: Visitors can use the pressure-wash bay next to the boatyard for a flat fee of €10 [S2].
rationale: No passage mentions a pressure-wash bay or any boat-washing facility.

question: How many nights does a visiting boat pay for when it stays 7 nights in a row at Gullstone?
statement: [S1] A visiting boat that stays for 7 consecutive nights is billed for only 6 of them.
rationale: S1 says a visitor who stays 7 nights in a row pays for only 6.

question: May a Gullstone berth holder sub-let their berth?
statement: Yes, berth holders may sub-let their berth, although swaps can only be arranged through the marina office [S5].
rationale: S5 says sub-letting a berth is not allowed, so the main claim reverses the passage.

question: What is the maximum shore power supply at each Gullstone berth?
statement: The maximum supply is sixteen amps per berth [S2].
rationale: S2 gives a maximum of 16 amps per berth, the same value written as a number word.

question: Whom should a cruising club contact before bringing a rally to Gullstone?
statement: Cruising clubs and rallies should contact the Harbour Master, Captain Rafael Okoro-Lunn, at least 4 weeks before arrival [S3].
rationale: S3 names the Events Coordinator, Mateus Sandoval-Obi, as the contact, while Captain Rafael Okoro-Lunn is the Harbour Master in S1.

question: What third-party insurance must a vessel with a Gullstone annual berth have?
statement: Every vessel needs third-party liability cover of no less than €3,000,000, and berth holders must send a copy of the certificate to the marina office before 1 April each year [S4].
rationale: S4 requires third-party liability insurance of at least €3,000,000 and a yearly copy of the certificate sent to the office before 1 April.

question: How much deposit is needed to join the Gullstone berth waiting list?
statement: [S2] Joining the waiting list costs a €200 deposit, which is taken off the first licence fee when a berth is offered.
rationale: S2 sets the waiting list deposit at €250, not €200.

question: Does Gullstone give berth holders a discount for paying the annual licence fee early?
statement: Berth holders who pay the full licence fee before 1 March receive a 5% early-payment discount [S1].
rationale: The passages mention a 4% surcharge for monthly payment but no discount for paying early.

question: What credit can a Gullstone berth holder earn when visitors use the berth during an absence?
statement: If you report an absence of at least 7 nights, you are credited 20% of the visitor fees earned on your berth, up to a ceiling of €300 per licence year, and the credit goes on your next licence invoice [S3].
rationale: S3 gives a credit of 20% of visitor fees for reported absences of 7 nights or more, up to €300 per licence year, applied to the next invoice.

question: At what time is tea served at Bramblecot?
statement: At Bramblecot, tea is served at 4 pm [S1].
rationale: S1 says tea is at 16:00, which is the same time as 4 pm.

question: Which Bramblecot room has a ratio of one adult to every 4 children?
statement: The Seedlings room, for babies aged 6 months to 2 years, has one adult for every 4 children [S3].
rationale: S3 gives the 1-to-4 ratio to the Saplings room, while the Seedlings room has one adult for every 3 children.

question: Whose fees does the Bramblecot sibling discount reduce, and what does it exclude?
statement: When two or more children from one family attend at the same time, 10% comes off the older child's fees; the discount is not applied to funded hours or extra sessions [S5].
rationale: S5 says the 10% sibling discount is taken off the older child's fees and does not apply to funded hours or extra sessions.

question: Does Bramblecot reduce fees for days a child is off sick?
statement: Yes, fees are reduced for days a child misses because of sickness [S1].
rationale: S1 states that fees are not reduced for sickness, so the statement reverses it.

question: How long must a Bramblecot child stay away from nursery after a bout of vomiting?
statement: After vomiting or diarrhoea, a child must stay away from nursery until 48 hours after the last episode [S2].
rationale: S2 contains this rule word for word.

question: What does a morning session cost at Bramblecot for a child aged 2 or over?
statement: For children aged 2 and over, a morning session costs £36.50 [S1].
rationale: S1 prices the morning session for children aged 2 and over at £38.50, not £36.50.

question: Does Bramblecot offer a minibus service to bring children to the nursery?
statement: Bramblecot runs a minibus pick-up for children in the Oaks room at £3.00 per trip [S2].
rationale: No passage mentions any minibus or transport service.

question: Who may collect a child from Bramblecot Day Nursery?
statement: [S1] Children are only handed over to adults aged 16 or over who are named on the registration form; if somebody else needs to collect, parents must phone the nursery beforehand and give that person the family password, without which staff will not release the child.
rationale: S1 limits collection to named adults aged 16 or over and requires a phone call in advance and the family password for anyone else.

question: How much is the non-refundable fee Bramblecot charges when a place is accepted?
statement: When a place is accepted, parents pay a registration fee of fifty pounds, which is not refundable [S3].
rationale: S3 gives a non-refundable registration fee of £50, the same value as fifty pounds.

question: May Bramblecot staff use their mobile phones in the children's rooms?
statement: Staff may use mobile phones in the children's rooms, although photos of children are taken only on nursery tablets [S5].
rationale: S5 says staff may not use mobile phones in any of the children's rooms, so the main claim reverses it.

question: By which day of the month must Bramblecot fees be paid?
statement: Fees are invoiced monthly in advance and must be paid by the 10th of each month [S2].
rationale: S2 says fees must be paid by the 5th of each month, not the 10th.

question: What is Bramblecot's late collection charge, and can funded hours be put towards it?
statement: Late collection costs £15 for every 15 minutes, or part of 15 minutes, after 18:30 [S2], and funded hours cannot be used to pay that charge [S4].
rationale: S2 gives the £15 charge per 15 minutes or part after 18:30 and S4 says funded hours cannot be used for the late collection charge.

question: What training do Bramblecot key persons have?
statement: Every key person holds an early years qualification and a current paediatric first aid certificate [S2].
rationale: The passages describe the key person's role but say nothing about qualifications or first aid training.
